newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Call selling in T-bonds as uptrend stalls.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Call selling in T-bonds as uptrend stalls.

text.p: Traders sold call options on U.S. Treasury bond futures from the outset Thursday, depressing volatility and suggesting to some that the bull market could be getting wobbly, floor traders said.

The increased interest in selling calls marks a shift from the past two sessions, which saw call purchases pick up as the underlying futures soared to their highest level in 1-1/2 years, traders said.
This morning, one investment firm sold 1,000 September 115-00 calls near the open, knocking volatility back, said a floor broker.
A brokerage house also sold 1,000 calls each in the 116-00 and 117-00 strikes in September.
Implied volatility for September options opened at 7.90 percent, down slightly from the previous settlement, and was quoted at 7.75 percent toward the end of the session.
September bond futures settled 2/32 lower at 115-10/32.
Market participants had expected volatility to be scaled back in the wake of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to Congress, which concluded Wednesday.
But options traders said next week's heavy lineup of economic data could revive interest rate volatility somewhat.
"You'd think it should go up a little bit. Those are major reports," said one Eurodollar broker.
The U.S. second-quarter employment cost index is due out Tuesday, followed on Thursday by advance second-quarter gross domestic product and on Friday by July employment.

This Friday, June durable goods orders and existing home sales will be reported. Analysts expect durable orders to rise 1.4 percent vs a 0.6 percent drop in May. Home sales are seen slowing to a 4.19 million annualized rate from 4.24 million.
As volatility slipped in Treasury bonds, one dealer stepped in to buy 5,000 September 115-00 calls covered against futures sold at 115-05.
"It's a pure volatility play," the bond trader said.
Any pop in vols could be temporary given the serene fundamental outlook, analysts cautioned.

"It is likely that a week from tomorrow, volatility will be lower than it is today," said John Nyhoff, chief economist for Toyko-Mitsubishi Futures (USA) Inc on the floor of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
December Eurodollar futures are pricing in about a 35-40 percent chance of a 25-basis-point rate tightening by year end, Nyhoff noted.
December straddle volatility finished steady on the day at 9.0 percent in the 94.00 strike, with March 94.00 also flat at 11.0 percent, according to one options desk.
Activity in Eurodollar options focused on put buying, with one dealer notable for purchasing 3,000 October 93.75 puts.
